description: methodology 1.5 — the rating-orthogonality penalty: the shipped per-tail form against the whole-axis form, against the penalty removed, against a free control carrying neither the penalty nor the teaching pull. The claims: a whole-axis penalty is a LINEAR statistic and cannot see a symmetric tail dependence, so that arm reports small whole-axis correlations while its axis ENDS — the only part a name is read off — stay rating-laden several-fold higher; scoring the two ends separately cuts the worst end to a fraction of that; with the penalty off the axes absorb the shipped per-problem quantities; and the free control spends an axis on a shipped parameter outright, the doc's signature being its correlation with SLOPE rather than with difficulty. EVERY ARM RUNS AT TWO SEEDS. The leak statistics are per-fit properties and the held-out contrast is paired within a seed, and both need a replicate for the same reason: the shipped configuration's own held-out score wanders wider across the closing third of a run than the contrast this panel is asked about, and a per-fit tail statistic has no error bar at all from one fit. Across seeds nothing is subtracted; within a seed every arm holds aside the same rows. A `rating_only` arm keeps the shipped per-tail form and narrows the target to the rating alone: it is the displacement claim's own arm, since closing one channel is only a partial closure if each axis then finds another shipped quantity to absorb.
